text:
Carolina attempted 79 shots to Philadelphia's 43, put 40 on goal against 18, and still needed overtime to get out of Xfinity Mobile Arena with a 3-2 win. The chance quality backs up the volume: CAR created 4.79 expected goals to PHI's 2.83, and in a simulated replay of every shot the Hurricanes win 78 percent of the time. The second period was the clearest picture of it, a 2.78 to 0.53 edge in expected goals that produced only a Matvei Michkov wrist shot at the other end, a 26 percent chance that put the Flyers up 2-1.

Joseph Woll is the reason it stayed that close. He faced 40 shots and allowed three on 4.79 expected goals, stopping 1.79 more than an average goalie would have. Sebastian Aho scored 10 seconds into the game, but Owen Tippett answered in the first period, and Carolina then spent the middle frame pressing without a goal to show for it. Pyotr Kochetkov, with just 18 shots to handle, was also a touch better than expected, saving 0.83 goals above the model.

The power play finally broke it open. Aho tied the game at 4:59 of the third on the man advantage, a snap shot assisted by Nikolaj Ehlers and Andrei Svechnikov. In overtime, Shayne Gostisbehere ended it with a slap shot at 2:51, again on a power play, with Jackson Blake and Aho setting it up. Carolina went 2 for 4 with the extra man while Philadelphia went 0 for 4, and that was the difference on a night the Flyers were outplayed by a wide margin.
